barriers.description: Usability testing with patients was conducted virtually due to COVID-19, which prevented observation of nonverbal cues during sessions.
barriers.justification: The inability to observe nonverbal behavior limited researchers' ability to fully manage user understanding and to evaluate users' interactions and emotional responses during testing, hindering evaluation and context-of-use studies.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, usability testing sessions were conducted using videoconferencing software (Zoom Video Communications Inc). Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, usability testing sessions conducted with patients were virtual and nonverbal cues could not be observed; however, screen sharing along with open-ended questions allowed us to obtain sufficient feedback which was often consistent across participants.

barriers.description: FH Family Share was not integrated with the electronic health record, limiting ease of access across remote or underserved communities with diverse EHR systems.
barriers.justification: Lack of EHR integration constrained designers' ability to study and support real-world contexts of use and to facilitate involvement of users in certain settings, thereby hindering understanding context of use and facilitating user involvement for deployment.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Additionally, FH Family Share was not integrated with the electronic health record to enable ease of access in remote or underserved communities which may have different electronic health record systems in place.

barriers.description: Usability testing was limited to genetic counselors and patients and did not include family members of patients.
barriers.justification: Excluding family members prevented designers from obtaining input from an important user group, limiting their ability to manage user understanding and to plan for implementation in nonclinical settings where family members are key actors.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Usability testing sessions were limited to genetic counselors and patients with familial hypercholesterolemia—input from family members of patients with familial hypercholesterolemia would be useful in ensuring effective implementation of the tool in nonclinical settings.
